clue.text: Lover of Scotland's back to back articles making a grand?

parts.note: jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart
the indefinite article

indicators.note: two things back to back face opposite ways, so the second copy is turned round

parts.note: the same article again, to be turned round

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's sweetheart trades articles back to back to raise a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A grand' looks like a thousand pounds, but it is a grand piano. JOANNA is old rhyming slang for piano, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano, and a grand is one kind of piano.

clue.text: Pool ball's on top of pocket

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on top of another simply comes first

parts.note: the jack is the small target ball in bowls
to pot a ball is to sink it into a pocket

explanation.surface: A snooker or pool player's ball sits on the edge of a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool, ball and pocket all point to the table game, but 'Pool' is the definition: a pooled stake, as in a lottery. The jack is the target ball in bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a combined fund of stakes, and the accumulated prize money in a lottery or game is called the jackpot.

clue.text: Brightest star has finally dropped behind mountain

indicators.note: the word's final letter is dropped, leaving the rest
in a down entry, coming behind means following the other part

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
the word written out, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: The brightest star in the sky has sunk behind a mountain peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Astronomers label the brightest star in a constellation with the first Greek letter, so ALPHA Centauri is the brightest in Centaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars in a constellation are ranked by Greek letter, so the label for the most luminous one is the first letter of that alphabet.

clue.text: On pest being uncovered, without delay put up traps

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits above it and is read first
in a down entry, putting something up writes it bottom to top

parts.note: without delay means soon

indicators.note: uncovering strips the outer covering, so only the inner letters remain

parts.note: the inner pair of letters once the outside two are removed

explanation.surface: A pest is exposed, and someone quickly sets traps for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' opens the clue like a preposition about the pest, but it is a placement signal: the turned-round word for promptly goes on top of the pest's core.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a running loop of rope or wire that tightens when pulled, used as a snare for animals.

clue.text: Stay supportive of nasty piece of work

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a rogue is a dishonest rascal

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to remain loyal to a thoroughly unpleasant person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' reads as remain, but here it is the legal verb meaning suspend or postpone, as in a stay of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a parliament is to suspend its sitting without dissolving it, a legal postponement like a court's order to halt proceedings.

clue.text: Like some poetry by Frost, recited at bar

indicators.note: reciting is speaking a word out, so we want its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: rime is hoar frost
bar in its sense of except, as is less

explanation.surface: Poems by Robert Frost being performed in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the poet Robert Frost, ideal for a poetry clue, but it is plain frozen dew, rime. 'Bar' looks like a pub; it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Blank verse and free verse have lines that do not chime at their ends, so such poetry has no rhyme.

clue.text: Everything deposited beneath base of cliff, following shock?

definitions.text: Everything deposited beneath base of cliff, following shock?

indicators.note: in a down entry, lying beneath something means coming after it
what follows is placed after the earlier piece

parts.note: to rock someone is to shake or shock them

indicators.note: the base of a down word is its bottom, which is the last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
all means everything

explanation.surface: After a tremor, debris piles up at the foot of a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read normally, it describes the heap of debris left after a tremor shakes a cliff face loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockfall is a mass of stones breaking off a cliff and landing at its foot, often set off by an earthquake or other jolt.

clue.text: Travel around islands working out musical direction

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: working something out rearranges it, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller tours the islands while planning a route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' suggests a compass heading for the island trip, but it is an instruction written on a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissando is an instruction in a score telling the player to slide continuously through a run of notes.

clue.text: Revised pieces checked by one editor after another

indicators.note: a second copy placed after the first is simply added at the end
something checked is held back or restrained, so it sits inside the restraining piece

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
chess or draughts pieces are called men
a second editor, abbreviated the same way

explanation.surface: Articles are checked and revised by a succession of editors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' reads as newspaper articles, fitting the editors, but it means the men of a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, so a revised text has been altered in this way.

clue.text: Nora Batty's a nag

indicators.note: batty means crazy, a sign of letters scrambled out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nora Batty, the formidable housewife of the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, is called a nag.
explanation.walkthrough: Batty is her surname in the sitcom, so it reads as part of a name, but here it is the anagram signal. 'Nag' reads as a scold; it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an informal word for a horse, and a roan is a horse whose coat mixes white hairs with a darker colour.

clue.text: Professional record inhibited by modest use of obscenity

indicators.note: being inhibited means held in or restrained, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: coy means bashful or demure
a pro is a professional
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A professional's career record is held back by a prim reluctance to swear.
explanation.walkthrough: The bashful word wraps the two inner pieces, and the definition is the unusual term for preoccupation with filth.
explanation.definitionFit: Coprology is a preoccupation with filth or dirty language in writing and art, from Greek kopros meaning dung.

clue.text: Companion that is married wears ring

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: something worn is carried around the wearer, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A partner who is married wears a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring suggests a wedding band, matching married, but it is the verb for a bell sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: When a bell rings it chimes; both describe the clear tone produced by striking metal.

clue.text: Gradually introduce current after voicing concern

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other in the answer
voicing a word is saying it, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: to faze is to disturb or concern
in means fashionable, current

explanation.surface: A new electrical current is introduced slowly after someone raises safety worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts as electricity, which would usually give I or AC; here it means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To phase in a change is to bring it into effect step by step rather than all at once.

clue.text: Enemy forces at the Front, combined, poured forth

indicators.note: the front of each word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
fused means joined together

explanation.surface: Enemy troops at the front line join up and surge forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes 'the Front' look like a battlefront, but it just takes the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Effuse means to pour out or spill forth, as a liquid or a light, so its past tense matches.

clue.text: Gather food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fold or pleat fabric, a dressmaking term
second meaning: British slang for food, especially snacks at school

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to collect provisions. In British school slang tuck means snacks, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck is a stitched fold in cloth, like a gather, and British schoolchildren call their sweets and snacks tuck.

clue.text: More than one window sticks when installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: to cement is to glue or stick
as can mean when

explanation.surface: A window keeps jamming once it has been fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' reads as a window jamming; it is a verb meaning glues.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side, so the plural covers several windows.

clue.text: Stressed diner, due luncheon, extremely agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A hungry diner waiting for lunch is getting tense and agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stressed' suggests anxious, which suits the diner, but it means emphasised, as words are by a line drawn beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlining text gives it emphasis, so an underlined word is one the writer has emphasised.

clue.text: Shift scenery as required

indicators.note: to shift things is to move them about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stagehands are told to move the set when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift scenery' is what stagehands do between scenes, which hides that 'Shift' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessary and required are close synonyms, both meaning needed or essential.

clue.text: Going hungry about beginning of Eid? Quite the reverse

definitions.note: the definition is the opposite of the wordplay's meaning

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: fasting is going without food

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the festival's name

explanation.surface: Fasting around the start of Eid, the Muslim festival ending Ramadan, though in truth the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going hungry' looks like the definition, but it only builds the answer; the definition is 'Quite the reverse', the opposite of going hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of starving oneself is eating lavishly, which is what a banquet-goer does, and Eid itself ends Ramadan's fast with celebration meals.

clue.text: Nervous wreck in Spooner's depot supplying coffins?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so we swap them here

parts.note: a casket is a coffin; it takes the opening sound of the other word
a base is a depot; it takes the opening sound of the other word

explanation.surface: An emotional wreck works in a warehouse that supplies funeral coffins.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of casket and base, and a coffin store becomes the informal term for someone who cannot cope.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is informal for someone too anxious or overwhelmed to function, just like a nervous wreck.

clue.text: Newborn cat one's lost in garden city?

parts.note: a newborn is a baby

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
I is the Roman numeral one, removed here

explanation.surface: A newly born kitten goes missing in a leafy suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garden city' suggests a planned British town like Welwyn; the question mark points to ancient Babylon and its Hanging Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was famed for its Hanging Gardens, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

clue.text: Three seconds to illustrate problem on green?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, one second
s is the abbreviation for second
the abbreviation again, for the third

explanation.surface: A quick three-second demonstration of a tricky putt in golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three seconds' supplies three tiny units: an informal moment and two abbreviations. 'Green' looks like a golf green but is any lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Moss spreading through grass is a common nuisance for groundskeepers of lawns and bowling or putting surfaces.

clue.text: Warship essentially goes off tack

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central core, so we keep its middle letter

parts.note: the central letter of the seven
an egg that addles goes bad

explanation.surface: A warship changes course by tacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' looks like the sailing manoeuvre beside the warship, but it is horse equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is the collective term for a horse's riding equipment, chiefly the saddle and bridle.

clue.text: Husband picked up corsage containing small aromatic plant

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top
containing means holding within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a corsage is a small bunch of flowers
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A husband collects a corsage with a small fragrant flower in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as collected, which suits a husband fetching flowers; it means lifted, so the word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is a bushy herb of the mint family with scented leaves, used in cooking and medicine.

clue.text: Puzzles are not included in broadcast applications

indicators.note: something not included is left out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to beam a programme is to broadcast it
uses are applications
A is the symbol for are, a metric unit of area, removed here

explanation.surface: Puzzles are missing from the apps that broadcasters offer.
explanation.walkthrough: An are is a metric unit of 100 square metres, abbreviated A; taking it out of the joined broadcast and applications words leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse is to bewilder or confuse, and puzzles works as the same transitive verb.

clue.text: Lout lying about criminal youth

indicators.note: lying turned about faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a yob is a British hooligan
a hood is a gangster or criminal

explanation.surface: A thug lies about a young offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests telling untruths; it means stretched out the wrong way round. Yob is British slang for a lout, and it is itself boy spelt backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth as a period of life matches the time of being a boy, before adulthood.

clue.text: Support line missed by player in game

indicators.note: something missed is absent, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Black is one of the two sides in chess
L is the abbreviation for line, removed here

explanation.surface: A sports team's supporting player is missing from the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player in game' sounds like a sportsman; it is one of the two sides in chess or draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or cause is to support them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Amateur cutting old ruby with blades

indicators.note: something cutting into a word splits it and sits inside

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
A is the abbreviation for amateur
ruby is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A hobbyist gem-cutter shapes an antique ruby with sharp tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The blades suggest cutting tools for the gem, but they are the flat ends of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade is the flat end of an oar, so a boat fitted with them is oared.

clue.text: Bit of offal I found in Indian wrap

parts.note: lung is one of the organs sold as offal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a piece of offal inside an Indian takeaway wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' looks like a rolled flatbread, but it is a garment wrapped round the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth worn wrapped round the waist like a sarong in India and neighbouring countries.

clue.text: Rat cleans out family

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in a family home

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traitor clears out his own relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like a rodent or traitor and 'cleans out' like a robbery, but both words are just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A family seat or heirloom is an ancestral one, inherited down generations of kin.

clue.text: Bouquets console supplier quite disheartened following refusal

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter
what follows is placed after the earlier piece

parts.note: a refusal is a no
Sega is a Japanese maker of video game consoles
'Quite!' is an expression of agreement, like yes

explanation.surface: Flowers are sent to comfort a supplier who is downcast after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' reads as a verb to comfort, matching the flowers; it is a games machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of fragrant flowers, an old-fashioned word for a posy or bouquet.

clue.text: Suspicion of student clerics stealing rector's suit

indicators.note: a suspicion is a slight trace, so only a first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter only

indicators.note: something stolen is taken away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: padres are military chaplains
R is the abbreviation for rector, removed here

explanation.surface: A student suspects that clergymen have stolen a rector's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing worth stealing, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards, alongside hearts, diamonds and clubs.
